answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor every identity to a kernel of verifiable work: each agent must complete a costly, useful task - attesting peers' transactions - before its votes count. A newcomer starts on a narrow ledge: one identity, one vote, no history, so a thousand fake accounts cost a thousand times the compute and time. A public beacon publishes the work each identity has done, so the network spots cheap clones instantly and only long-lived, productive agents earn weight. Faking scale stops paying; doing real work becomes the only path in.
